_about: One short, checked fact per street/city ('<tile name>|<group code>') and per country or region (group code). Shown under a card as 'Did you know?'. Written and fact-checked 2026-10-14.

places.A Coruña|ES_GAL: A Coruña's Tower of Hercules is a Roman lighthouse built nearly 2,000 years ago that still guides ships today.
places.Abu Dhabi|AE: Abu Dhabi is the capital of the UAE and home to the Louvre Abu Dhabi, a museum sheltered under a vast lace-like dome.
places.Abuja|NG: Abuja became Nigeria's capital in 1991, taking over from Lagos, and is overlooked by Aso Rock, a giant granite monolith.
places.Accra|GH: Accra's name comes from the Akan word Nkran, meaning ants, after the many anthills once seen in the countryside around it.
places.Addis Ababa|ET: Addis Ababa means 'new flower' in Amharic, and it sits so high in the Ethiopian Highlands that it is one of the world's highest capitals.
places.Adelaide|AU_SA: Adelaide was planned by Colonel William Light, and its city centre is completely surrounded by a ring of green parklands.
places.Agra|UP: Agra's Taj Mahal was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, and the city is famous for petha sweets.
places.Ahmedabad|GJ: In 2017 Ahmedabad's walled old city became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City, and its skies fill with kites every January.
places.Ahmedabad|IN_GJ: Ahmedabad became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City in 2017, and its sky fills with kites every January for Uttarayan.
places.Albuquerque|US_SW: Albuquerque hosts the International Balloon Fiesta every October, when hundreds of hot-air balloons fill the desert sky.
places.Alcalá de Henares|ES_MAD: Alcalá de Henares is the birthplace of Miguel de Cervantes, author of Don Quixote, and its historic university is UNESCO-listed.
places.Alexandria|EG: Alexandria was founded by Alexander the Great, and its ancient lighthouse, the Pharos, was one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
places.Alicante|ES_VAL: Alicante's palm-lined seafront promenade, the Explanada de España, is paved with millions of marble tiles in a wave pattern.
places.Alice Springs|AU_NT: Alice Springs hosts the Henley-on-Todd Regatta, a boat race on a dry riverbed where crews run carrying bottomless boats.
places.Amalfi|IT_CAM: Amalfi was a powerful sea-trading republic in the Middle Ages and is still famous for its handmade paper.
places.Amiens|FR_HDF: Jules Verne, author of Around the World in Eighty Days, spent his later life in Amiens, where his house is now a museum.
places.Amsterdam|NL: Amsterdam's 17th-century canal ring is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and much of the city stands on wooden poles driven deep into the ground.
places.Ankara|TR: Ankara, not Istanbul, has been the capital of Turkey since 1923, and Atatürk's mausoleum, Anıtkabir, stands on a hill there.
places.Annecy|FR_ARA: Annecy is nicknamed the Venice of the Alps for its canals, and it hosts a famous international animation film festival every June.
places.Antalya|TR: Antalya, on the Turkish Riviera, has the Duden Waterfalls, which tumble off cliffs straight into the Mediterranean Sea.
places.Aomori|JP_TH: Aomori is famous for its apples, and every August its Nebuta Festival parades giant illuminated paper floats through the streets.
places.Apia|WS: Apia was the last home of Treasure Island author Robert Louis Stevenson, and his house, Vailima, is now a museum.
places.Arequipa|PE: Arequipa is called the White City because many buildings are made of sillar, a white volcanic stone, under El Misti volcano.
places.Arusha|TZ: Arusha sits at the foot of Mount Meru and is a popular starting point for safaris to the Serengeti and Ngorongoro Crater.
places.Athens|GR: Athens is named after the goddess Athena, and the Parthenon on its Acropolis was built in her honour about 2,500 years ago.
places.Auckland|NZ: Auckland is nicknamed the City of Sails and is built on a field of around 50 old volcanoes, including Mount Eden.
places.Augsburg|DE_BY: Augsburg's Fuggerei, set up by merchant Jakob Fugger in the 1500s, is the oldest social housing complex in the world still in use.
places.Auki|SB: Auki is the main town of Malaita, close to Langa Langa Lagoon, where islanders still make traditional shell money by hand.
places.Austin|US_TX: Austin calls itself the Live Music Capital of the World, and huge clouds of bats fly out from its Congress Avenue Bridge on summer evenings.
places.Ballarat|AU_VIC: Ballarat boomed in the 1850s gold rush, and its Sovereign Hill park recreates the old town, with gold panning for visitors.
places.Banff|CA_AB: Banff National Park, created in 1885, is Canada's first national park and is famous for turquoise lakes like Lake Louise.
places.Bangkok|TH: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world, and Thai people call the city Krung Thep.
places.Barcelona|ES: Barcelona is full of Antoni Gaudí's buildings, including the Sagrada Família and Park Güell with its colourful mosaic dragon.
places.Barcelona|ES_CAT: Barcelona is famous for Antoni Gaudí's buildings, from the Sagrada Família basilica, begun in 1882, to colourful Park Güell.
places.Bari|IT_PUG: In Bari's old town, local women make orecchiette pasta by hand at tables set out in the street outside their homes.
places.Beijing|CN: Beijing's Forbidden City was the palace of Chinese emperors for almost 500 years and contains around 980 buildings.
places.Beijing|CN_JH: Beijing is the first city to have hosted both the Summer Olympics, in 2008, and the Winter Olympics, in 2022.
places.Belconnen|AU_ACT: Belconnen is home to the Australian Institute of Sport, where many of the country's top athletes have trained.
places.Belém|BR_AMZ: Belém's riverside Ver-o-Peso market takes its name, meaning see the weight, from a colonial post where goods were weighed for tax.
places.Belfast|GB_NI: C.S. Lewis, author of The Chronicles of Narnia, was born in Belfast in 1898, and the city's C.S. Lewis Square has statues of Narnia characters.
places.Belfast|IE: Belfast is the birthplace of C.S. Lewis, author of The Chronicles of Narnia, and has a square full of Narnia sculptures.
places.Belo Horizonte|BR_MG: Belo Horizonte, meaning beautiful horizon, is home to Pampulha, a lakeside group of early Oscar Niemeyer buildings listed by UNESCO.
places.Bengaluru|IN: Bengaluru is nicknamed India's Silicon Valley for its tech companies and the Garden City for green spaces like Lalbagh.
places.Bengaluru|IN_SI: Bengaluru is called the Silicon Valley of India, and its Lalbagh garden holds a famous flower show twice a year.
places.Bengaluru|KA: Bengaluru is called the Silicon Valley of India for its tech companies and the Garden City for green spaces like Lalbagh.
places.Bergamo|IT_LOM: Bergamo's hilltop upper town, the Città Alta, is ringed by UNESCO-listed Venetian walls and reached by a funicular railway.
places.Berlin|DE: The currywurst snack was invented in Berlin in 1949, when Herta Heuwer mixed ketchup and curry powder into a sauce for sausages.
places.Berlin|DE_BB: Berlin's favourite snack, currywurst, was first sold there in 1949 by Herta Heuwer from her street stall.
places.Bhubaneswar|EA: Bhubaneswar is called the Temple City of India, with hundreds of carved stone temples such as the ancient Lingaraja Temple.
places.Bhubaneswar|IN_EC: Bhubaneswar, nicknamed the Temple City, was laid out as a modern capital by German architect Otto Königsberger in the 1940s.
places.Biarritz|FR_NAQ: Biarritz became a fashionable resort after Empress Eugénie, wife of Napoleon III, built a seaside palace there in the 1850s.
places.Bilbao|ES_EUS: Bilbao's shimmering titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum, designed by Frank Gehry, opened in 1997 and made the city world famous.
places.Birmingham|GB_MID: Cadbury chocolate began in Birmingham, where John Cadbury opened his shop in 1824; the Bournville factory village followed.
places.Birmingham|UK: Birmingham is the home of Cadbury chocolate, made at Bournville, a leafy village the Cadbury family built for its workers.
places.Birmingham|US_DS: Birmingham, Alabama, is nicknamed the Magic City, and its giant Vulcan statue is the largest cast-iron statue in the world.
places.Blackpool|GB_NW: Blackpool Tower, which opened in 1894, was inspired by the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
places.Bocas del Toro|PA: Bocas del Toro is an island chain on Panama's Caribbean coast, known for coral reefs, starfish beaches and tiny red frogs.
places.Bogotá|CO: Bogotá sits about 2,600 metres up in the Andes, making it one of the highest capital cities in the world.
places.Bologna|IT: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is considered the oldest university in continuous operation in the world.
places.Bologna|IT_EMR: Bologna is nicknamed 'La Grassa' (the fat one) for its rich food, and its long arched porticoes are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.Bordeaux|FR_NAQ: Bordeaux is famous for canelés, small caramelised pastries, and its Port of the Moon riverside is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.Boston|US: Boston Common, set aside in 1634, is the oldest city park in the United States, and Boston also opened America's first subway.
places.Boston|US_NE: Boston opened America's first subway in 1897, and Boston Common, dating from 1634, is the country's oldest city park.
places.Brasília|BR_CO: Brasília was built from scratch and became Brazil's capital in 1960, and its city plan is shaped like an airplane.
places.Brasov|RO: Brasov's Rope Street, Strada Sforii, is one of the narrowest streets in Europe, only a little over a metre wide in places.
places.Bremen|DE_HAN: A bronze statue in Bremen shows the Town Musicians from the Grimm fairy tale: a donkey, dog, cat and rooster stacked up.
places.Brest|FR_BRE: Brest hosts a giant maritime festival where hundreds of traditional sailing ships from around the world fill its harbour.
places.Brighton|GB_SE: Brighton's Royal Pavilion was built as a seaside palace for the Prince Regent, later George IV, in an Indian-inspired style.
places.Brisbane|AU_QLD: Brisbane's Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary opened in 1927 and is recognised as the world's first koala sanctuary.
places.Bucharest|RO: Bucharest was nicknamed Little Paris for its elegant boulevards and buildings, and it even has its own Arc de Triomphe.
places.Buenos Aires|AR: Buenos Aires helped give birth to the tango, and its Avenida 9 de Julio is one of the widest city avenues in the world.
places.Burgos|ES_CYL: Burgos Cathedral, a UNESCO-listed Gothic masterpiece, holds the tomb of the legendary Castilian knight El Cid.
places.Busan|KR: Busan is South Korea's biggest port, and its Jagalchi Fish Market is one of the country's best-known seafood markets.
places.Byron Bay|AU_NSW: Cape Byron, next to Byron Bay, is the most easterly point of mainland Australia and is topped by a lighthouse first lit in 1901.
places.Cáceres|ES_EXT: Cáceres has a beautifully preserved walled old town full of medieval towers and palaces, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.Cairns|AU_QLD: Cairns is a gateway to two World Heritage Sites: the Great Barrier Reef and the ancient Daintree Rainforest.
places.Cairo|EG: Cairo sits on the banks of the River Nile, and the Great Pyramids of Giza stand at the edge of the greater city.
places.Calgary|CA_AB: Every July, Calgary hosts the Calgary Stampede, a ten-day rodeo and festival nicknamed the Greatest Outdoor Show on Earth.
places.Cambridge|UK: The double-helix shape of DNA was worked out at Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory in 1953 by Francis Crick and James Watson.
places.Campinas|BR_SP: Campinas is the birthplace of composer Carlos Gomes, whose opera Il Guarany was a hit at Milan's La Scala in 1870.
places.Campo Grande|BR_CO: Campo Grande is nicknamed the Cidade Morena, or Brown City, because of the reddish-brown colour of its soil.
places.Canberra|AU_ACT: Canberra was designed by American architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin after they won a 1912 competition.
places.Cancún|MX: Cancún's underwater museum, MUSA, has hundreds of statues on the seabed that are slowly turning into coral reefs.
places.Cannes|FR_PAC: Cannes hosts a world-famous film festival every May, when stars climb the red-carpeted steps of the Palais des Festivals.
places.Cape Town|ZA: Cape Town lies beneath flat-topped Table Mountain, which is often draped in a layer of cloud nicknamed the 'tablecloth'.
places.Cardiff|GB_CYM: Cardiff was proclaimed the capital of Wales in 1955, and its city-centre castle stands on the site of a Roman fort.
places.Cartagena|CO: Cartagena's old town is ringed by colonial stone walls, and its colourful streets are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.Casablanca|MA: Casablanca means 'white house' in Spanish, and the city is the setting of the classic 1942 Hollywood film Casablanca.
places.Catania|IT_SIC: Catania sits at the foot of Mount Etna, and many of its Baroque buildings are made from dark volcanic lava stone.
places.Changchun|CN_DB: Changchun, whose name means 'long spring', is a big centre of China's car industry and home to a famous film studio.
places.Changsha|CN_HZ: Changsha is known for fiery Hunan cooking and stinky tofu, and its long Orange Isle sits in the middle of the Xiang River.
places.Charlottetown|CA_MR: Charlottetown is called the Birthplace of Confederation because the 1864 meeting that led to the creation of Canada was held there.
places.Chemnitz|DE_SN: Chemnitz was nicknamed the 'Saxon Manchester' for its many textile mills and machine factories in the 1800s.
places.Chengdu|CN_XN: Chengdu is famous for giant pandas, spicy Sichuan food and teahouses, and was named a UNESCO City of Gastronomy.
places.Chennai|IN_SI: Chennai's Marina Beach, running along the Bay of Bengal, is the longest natural city beach in India and a favourite evening spot.
places.Chennai|TN: Chennai's Marina Beach, running along the Bay of Bengal, is one of the longest city beaches in the world.
places.Chiang Mai|TH: Chiang Mai's old city is ringed by a square moat, and every year it lights up the sky with lanterns during the Yi Peng festival.
places.Chicago|US: Engineers reversed the flow of the Chicago River in 1900, so it now runs away from Lake Michigan instead of into it.
places.Chicago|US_GL: Chicago's shiny Cloud Gate sculpture, nicknamed The Bean, is made of 168 stainless steel plates welded together.
places.Chongqing|CN_XN: Chongqing is famous for numbing-spicy hotpot, and at Liziba station one of its monorail lines runs right through an apartment block.
places.Christchurch|NZ: Christchurch is nicknamed the Garden City, and flat-bottomed punts glide along the Avon River past its Botanic Gardens.
places.Cienfuegos|CU: Cienfuegos is nicknamed the 'Pearl of the South', and its French-founded historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.Cleveland|US_GL: Cleveland is home to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, housed in a glass pyramid designed by architect I. M. Pei.
places.Cluj|RO: Cluj-Napoca is called the unofficial capital of Transylvania and is home to Babeș-Bolyai, Romania's largest university.
places.Coimbatore|TN: Coimbatore is called the Manchester of South India because of its many cotton textile mills.
places.Colmar|FR_GES: Colmar's Little Venice district has canals lined with colourful houses, and Statue of Liberty sculptor Bartholdi was born there.
places.Cologne|DE: Eau de Cologne, the famous fragrance, is named after Cologne, where perfumer Johann Maria Farina created it in 1709.
places.Colón|PA: Colón sits at the Caribbean entrance of the Panama Canal and is home to a huge free trade zone.
places.Como|IT_LOM: Como, on the shore of Lake Como, is the hometown of Alessandro Volta, inventor of the electric battery and namesake of the volt.
places.Concepción|CL: Concepción is often called the cradle of Chilean rock, as bands such as Los Tres and Los Bunkers started out there.
places.Coober Pedy|AU_SA: Coober Pedy is famous for opals, and many locals live in underground homes called dugouts to escape the outback heat.
places.Córdoba|AR: Córdoba is nicknamed La Docta, the learned one, thanks to its university founded in 1613, one of the oldest in the Americas.
places.Cork|IE: Cork is Ireland's second-largest city, and nearby Blarney Castle holds the Blarney Stone, said to give the gift of the gab to all who kiss it.
places.Corner Brook|CA_NL: Corner Brook overlooks the Bay of Islands, which Captain James Cook mapped in 1767, and a monument to him stands above the city.
places.Cuenca|EC: Cuenca is a major centre for weaving toquilla straw hats, which are better known around the world as Panama hats.
places.Cuiabá|BR_CO: Cuiabá has a monument marking the spot calculated as the geodesic centre of South America, far from both oceans.
places.Curitiba|BR_SUL: Curitiba's fast bus network, with its glass tube-shaped stations, inspired similar bus rapid transit systems around the world.
places.Cusco|PE: Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire, and today it is the main starting point for trips to Machu Picchu.
places.Da Nang|VN: Da Nang's Golden Bridge in the Ba Na Hills looks as if it is being held up by two giant stone hands.
places.Dallas|US_TX: The integrated circuit, the chip inside modern electronics, was invented by Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments in Dallas in 1958.
places.Dar es Salaam|TZ: Dar es Salaam's name comes from Arabic and is usually translated as 'house of peace' or 'haven of peace'.
places.Darwin|AU_NT: Darwin is named after naturalist Charles Darwin; in 1839 his former shipmates on HMS Beagle named the harbour Port Darwin.
places.Denpasar|ID: Denpasar is the capital of Bali, and its Bali Museum showcases traditional Balinese art, masks and crafts in palace-style buildings.
places.Denver|US_MW: Denver is the Mile High City, and one step of its State Capitol is marked as exactly one mile above sea level.
places.Derry|GB_NI: Derry's 17th-century city walls, about a mile around, are the only complete set of town walls surviving in Ireland.
places.Detroit|US_GL: Detroit is nicknamed the Motor City for its car industry, and it gave the world the Motown sound of the 1960s.
places.Devonport|AU_TAS: Devonport is the Tasmanian home port of the Spirit of Tasmania ferries, which sail across Bass Strait to Victoria.
places.Dortmund|DE_NW: Dortmund's stadium is famous for the Yellow Wall, a giant standing terrace of Borussia Dortmund fans dressed in yellow.
places.Dresden|DE_SN: Dresden is nicknamed 'Florence on the Elbe' for its grand Baroque buildings and art collections along the River Elbe.
places.Dubai|AE: Dubai is home to the Burj Khalifa, which became the world's tallest building when it opened in 2010.
places.Dublin|IE: Dublin is a UNESCO City of Literature and the birthplace of writers including Oscar Wilde, Bram Stoker and James Joyce.
places.Dundee|GB_SCO: Dundee is famed for the 'three Js' of jute, jam and journalism, and The Beano comic is published there.
places.Durham|GB_NE: Durham Cathedral and Castle form a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the cathedral's cloisters appeared as Hogwarts in Harry Potter films.
places.Düsseldorf|DE_NW: Düsseldorf's elegant Königsallee boulevard, known locally as the Kö, runs along a tree-lined canal in the city centre.
places.Edinburgh|GB_SCO: Edinburgh Castle stands on Castle Rock, the plug of an extinct volcano, and nearby Arthur's Seat is an ancient volcano too.
places.Edmonton|CA_AB: West Edmonton Mall has an indoor wave pool, an ice rink and a theme park, and was once the largest mall in the world.
places.Eilat|IL: Eilat sits at the southern tip of Israel on the Red Sea, and its coral reefs begin just a few steps from the beach.
places.Elche|ES_VAL: Elche is home to the Palmeral, a huge grove of date palms first laid out in Moorish times and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.Fes|MA: The old medina of Fes is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for its maze of narrow alleys and colourful Chouara leather tannery.
places.Firenze|IT_TOS: Florence is called the cradle of the Renaissance, and Brunelleschi's great red-tiled cathedral dome still rules its skyline.
places.Florianópolis|BR_SUL: Most of Florianópolis sits on Santa Catarina Island, linked to the mainland by the Hercílio Luz suspension bridge, opened in 1926.
places.Fortaleza|BR_NE: Fortaleza means fortress in Portuguese, and the city grew up around a 17th-century fort on the Atlantic coast.
places.Frankfurt|DE: Frankfurt's skyscraper skyline on the River Main earned it the nickname Mainhattan, and the writer Goethe was born in the city.
places.Frankfurt|DE_HE: Frankfurt's cluster of skyscrapers beside the River Main has earned the city the nickname 'Mainhattan'.
places.Freiburg|DE_BW: Freiburg's old town is laced with Bächle, little water channels in the streets; legend says stepping in one means marrying a local.
places.Fremantle|AU_WA: The cool sea breeze that blows into Fremantle and Perth on hot summer afternoons is nicknamed the Fremantle Doctor.
places.Fukuoka|JP_KY: Fukuoka is the home of Hakata tonkotsu ramen and is famous for yatai, open-air food stalls that pop up along its streets at night.
places.Geelong|AU_VIC: Geelong's waterfront is dotted with dozens of colourful painted bollards, each showing a character from the city's past.
places.Girona|ES_CAT: Girona's colourful houses hang over the Onyar River, and its old town is still partly ringed by medieval stone walls.
places.Gizo|SB: Gizo, the capital of the Solomon Islands' Western Province, is a popular base for diving and surfing among coral reefs.
places.Glasgow|GB_SCO: Glasgow's circular Subway opened in 1896 and is affectionately nicknamed the Clockwork Orange for its bright orange trains.
places.Glasgow|UK: Glasgow's Subway, opened in 1896, is the third-oldest underground metro in the world and is nicknamed the Clockwork Orange.
places.Gold Coast|AU_QLD: Surfers Paradise on the Gold Coast took its name from the Surfers Paradise Hotel, which opened there in 1925.
places.Gondar|ET: Gondar's royal enclosure, Fasil Ghebbi, is full of 17th-century castles, earning the city the nickname the Camelot of Africa.
places.Granada|ES_AND: Granada is home to the Alhambra, a stunning Moorish palace and fortress set against the snowy peaks of the Sierra Nevada.
places.Grenoble|FR_ARA: Grenoble hosted the 1968 Winter Olympics, and its round cable cars, nicknamed 'les bulles' (the bubbles), climb up to the Bastille fort.
places.Guadalajara|MX: Guadalajara is famous for mariachi music, which grew up in its home state of Jalisco, and hosts a big mariachi festival.
places.Guangzhou|CN_PRD: Guangzhou is nicknamed the City of Rams, after a legend of five immortals who arrived riding rams and carrying rice.
places.Guayaquil|EC: Guayaquil's Seminario Park is nicknamed Iguana Park because large green iguanas roam freely there among visitors.
places.Gungahlin|AU_ACT: Canberra's first light rail line, opened in 2019, runs from the Gungahlin town centre all the way to the city centre.
places.Gurugram|IN_DL: Gurugram, known as Gurgaon until 2016, is home to Cyber City, a cluster of glass towers housing many global companies.
places.Guwahati|EA: Guwahati sits on the banks of the mighty Brahmaputra River and is known as the Gateway to Northeast India.
places.Guwahati|IN_NE: Guwahati stands on the banks of the mighty Brahmaputra River and is known as the gateway to Northeast India.
places.Haifa|IL: Haifa's Carmelit is an underground funicular railway climbing Mount Carmel, and one of the shortest subway systems in the world.
places.Hakodate|JP_HK: Hakodate is known for Goryokaku, a star-shaped Western-style fort, and the glittering night view from the top of Mount Hakodate.
places.Halifax|CA_MR: A cannon is fired at noon from the Halifax Citadel almost every day of the year, a time-keeping tradition dating back to the 1850s.
places.Hamburg|DE: Hamburg's Speicherstadt is a UNESCO-listed warehouse district built on oak piles and crisscrossed by canals and bridges.
places.Hamburg|DE_HAN: Hamburg's Elbphilharmonie concert hall is a glittering glass building with a wavy roofline, set on top of an old brick warehouse.
places.Hangzhou|CN_JN: Hangzhou's West Lake has inspired poets and painters for centuries, and nearby hills grow famous Longjing (Dragon Well) tea.
places.Hanoi|VN: Many streets in Hanoi's Old Quarter are named after the goods once sold there, such as Hang Bac, or Silver Street.
places.Harbin|CN_DB: Harbin's winter Ice and Snow Festival features huge glowing buildings carved from blocks of ice cut from the Songhua River.
places.Havana|CU: Havana is famous for its colourful classic 1950s American cars and its long seaside promenade, the Malecón.
places.Heidelberg|DE_BW: Heidelberg University, founded in 1386, is the oldest university in Germany, and the castle ruins above it overlook the Neckar.
places.Hiroshima|JP_CG: Hiroshima has its own style of okonomiyaki, a savoury pancake layered with cabbage and noodles, and is near the island of Miyajima.
places.Hobart|AU_TAS: Hobart is the finish line of the Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race, which sets off from Sydney Harbour every Boxing Day.
places.Honiara|SB: Honiara, the capital of the Solomon Islands, sits on the north coast of Guadalcanal, the country's biggest island.
places.Hyderabad|IN_SI: Hyderabad, the City of Pearls, is famous for its biryani and the Charminar, a four-towered monument built in 1591.
places.Hyderabad|ME: Hyderabad's Charminar, built in 1591, has four grand arches and four tall minarets, and the city is famous for Hyderabadi biryani.
places.Ilhéus|BR_BA: Ilhéus grew rich on cocoa and is the setting of Jorge Amado's famous novel Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon.
places.Incheon|KR: Incheon is home to South Korea's main international airport, which was built on land reclaimed from the sea between islands.
places.Iqaluit|CA_NT: Iqaluit, the capital of Nunavut, means place of many fish in Inuktitut, and it was called Frobisher Bay until 1987.
places.Istanbul|TR: Istanbul is split by the Bosphorus Strait, so the city sits on two continents at once, Europe and Asia.
places.Izmir|TR: Izmir is Turkey's third-largest city, and the ruins of ancient Ephesus lie about an hour's drive to its south.
places.Jaipur|IN_RJ: Jaipur is the Pink City; its old town was painted pink to welcome the Prince of Wales on his visit in 1876.
places.Jaipur|RJ: Jaipur is called the Pink City because its old town was painted pink to welcome the Prince of Wales in 1876.
places.Jakarta|ID: Jakarta's National Monument, known as Monas, is a tall white tower topped with a flame covered in gold leaf.
places.Jerusalem|IL: By a long-standing city rule, buildings in Jerusalem are faced with Jerusalem stone, a pale limestone that glows gold at sunset.
places.Jodhpur|IN_RJ: Jodhpur is called the Blue City for its blue-painted houses clustered beneath the mighty Mehrangarh Fort.
places.Johannesburg|ZA: Johannesburg grew out of a gold rush in 1886 and is nicknamed Egoli, which means 'place of gold'.
places.Kagoshima|JP_KY: Kagoshima faces Sakurajima, an active volcano across the bay, and is nicknamed the 'Naples of the East' for the similar view.
places.Kalgoorlie|AU_WA: Kalgoorlie began with an 1893 gold rush after Paddy Hannan found gold there, and its main street is named Hannan Street after him.
places.Kanazawa|JP_CB: Kanazawa makes nearly all of Japan's gold leaf and is home to Kenroku-en, counted among the country's three great gardens.
places.Kano|NG: Kano's Kofar Mata dye pits, traditionally dated to 1498, are still used today to dye cloth a deep indigo blue.
places.Kansas City|US_HL: Kansas City is famous for slow-smoked barbecue and has so many fountains that it is called the City of Fountains.
places.Kashgar|CN_XB: Kashgar was a key oasis stop on the ancient Silk Road, where caravan routes from China, Central Asia and India met.
places.Kassel|DE_HE: The Brothers Grimm collected many of their famous fairy tales while living in Kassel, which now has a Grimm museum, Grimmwelt.
places.Kelowna|CA_BC: Kelowna sits on Okanagan Lake, home of the legendary Ogopogo lake monster, which has a statue on the city's waterfront.
places.Kingston|JM: Kingston is the home of reggae, and the Bob Marley Museum is in the singer's former house at 56 Hope Road.
places.Kisumu|KE: Kisumu sits on the shore of Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, and is Kenya's main port on the lake.
places.Kobe|JP_KS: Kobe gave its name to the famous marbled Kobe beef, which comes from Tajima cattle raised in the surrounding Hyogo Prefecture.
